This PACT CBOC Registered Nurse is located in the Nursing, Ambulatory Care service at the Somersworth, NH VA Clinic. This position is full-time at 40 hours per week.

Included but are not limited to: Plays an integral role in the Patient Aligned Care Team (PACT) providing initial and ongoing assessment of patients and functioning as a systems coordinator for the plan of care.

Initiates PACT preplanning for scheduled clinic visits, participates in daily huddle and team meetings to collaborate how best to meet the patients' needs. Conducts follow up calls to hospitalizations and Emergency Department visits, reviews records, and coordinates follow-up care.

Participates in direct patient care surrounding scheduled and unscheduled visits. Manages a designated panel of patients and utilizes VA developed protocols to enhance preventions as well as manage chronic diseases including HTN, DM, COPD, CHF.

Identifies and care manages high risk patients via face-to-face visits, virtual video connect, secure messaging, and telephone calls. - Coordinates transitions for patient care with specialists and consultants.

Conducts comprehensive assessment of patients' needs and ensures patients are linked with all appropriate services, resources and opportunities based on his or her needs.

Partners with Veteran to support self-management, prevention, and wellness, utilizing Health Coaching and Motivational Interviewing to assist with behavior change and guidance towards his or her goals. Provides patient-centered, evidence-based, patient driven care in all patient interactions across the care continuum.

Lab phlebotomy, point-of-care testing, and specimen labeling. Occasional travel may be required for education, organizational needs, or to provide nursing support at the other CBOC locations (Portsmouth, Tilton, Conway), or at the Manchester VA Medical Center. Work Schedule: Full-Time. Monday - Friday, 8:00am - 4:30pm. Telework: Not Available.

The Patient Safety Manager Lead (PSML) serves as a clinical and analytical expert responsible for coordinating patient safety activities across the organization. Supports a high-reliability culture through event review, risk identification, and proactive improvement efforts.

Responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care. Applies strong nursing informatics skills to create, analyze, and interpret safety reports; identify trends; monitor action plans; and support data-driven decision-making.

Demonstrates excellent judgment, and influences care outcomes by supporting education, leading improvement initiatives, and ensuring timely follow-up on safety events. PSM Lead supports and guides other Patient Safety Specialists, offering expertise, coaching, and guidance on patient safety priorities, methodologies, and data-driven practices.

Promote culturally competent care and reinforce a culture of accountability and high-quality, cost-effective outcomes. Maintains comprehensive knowledge of regulatory and accreditation standards, Directives, policies, and Standard Operating Procedures.

Leads initiatives to improve Veteran/patient experience, satisfaction and/or safety beyond the immediate practice setting. Communicates and collaborates as an effective leader of the interprofessional team, at the expert level, with improved evidence-based and/or data-driven outcomes beyond the immediate practice setting.

Meets the needs of the Veteran and as appropriate the Veteran's family, caregiver and/or significant other, the Veteran's representative, visitors to VA facilities, all VA staff and other customers while supporting VA missions.

Duties to include but are not limited to: Responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to primary care patients and oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the setting. Manages assigned panel(s), utilizes registries, and ensures appropriate evaluation and access is provided to patient panels.

Provides health promotion, health education and coaching on wellness, disease prevention, and chronic care management. Administers medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team.

Assists in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization. Applies clinical knowledge/judgment to lead staff involvement in planning, decision-making, and evaluating outcomes within the immediate practice setting.

Improves Veteran/patient driven care by resolving experience issues such as coordination of care, timeliness or process issues, common themes of dissatisfaction, or environment of care concerns for the immediate practice setting.

The Chief Nurse Perioperative Service (CN-PS) is important to the hierarchy of the Nursing Service structure in the continuum of care for the perioperative Veteran population.

This Chief Nurse supervises 8-Nurse Managers whose perioperative departments employees 215 staff members, and the Transplant program which incorporates the entire organization in its program.The CN-PS oversees the following units: Operating Rooms Day Surgery Procedure unit Interventional Radiology Post Anesthesia Care Unit Periop Specialty Units Non-Invasive Cardiology Invasive Cardiology Intervascular Team.

The Nurse IV CN-PS executes leadership that is characterized by substantial and continuous responsibility and accountability for population groups or integrated programs that cross services and/or discipline lines and influence the organizational healthcare mission.The Chief Nurse of Perioperative Programs functions as an advisor, administrator, educator, consultant, and mentor who possesses a wide range of experience and leadership ability.

Duties include but are not limited to: Assuming an appropriate degree of responsibility regarding administrative and clinical issues, such as Staff coverage, Granting leave, and Patient and/or staff issues; Working closely with the Peri-Operative Nurse Managers; Developing and implementing policies and practices that support high-quality healthcare delivery; Ensuring policies are followed by Registered Nurses (RN), Licensed Vocational Nurses (LVN), Nursing Assistants (NA), and Scrub Care Technicians within assigned units, etc.

The Assistant Nurse Manager (ANM) supports the Nurse Manager (NM) with supervisory duties and responsibility and accountability for the 24/7 operation of their designated units. They provide coverage for other ANMs as needed.

The ANM has responsibility and accountability for the direction and supervision of specific orientation, training, development of staff, and evaluation of individual staff performance. They function as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing leadership to the team.

They influence care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team to remove barriers and implement new evidence-based cutting-edge programs/processes. The ANM is expected to deliver patient care based on the needs of the unit. The ANM engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth.

They adhere to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. They equip staff with tools for culturally competent care and promotes a culture of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes.

They cultivate alliances across the care continuum, building trust through active listening, engagement, and emotional intelligence. The ANM contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable, and equitable patient care.

Ensures compliance with accreditation and regulatory standards. Aligns nursing/clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. They promote an inclusive workplace valuing diversity to achieve the organizations vision and mission.

The ANM maintains knowledge and ensures compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards, Directives, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOP).

The Assistant Nurse Manager, Patient Flow is responsible for facilitating the fulfillment of the VA Northern California Health Care System's mission, vision, values, and strategic direction within the Patient Flow department and as a member of the NCHCS leadership team.

The incumbent is an important facilitator of interdisciplinary effectiveness and communication that reaches outside of the department towards applicable community resources and relevant program offices within the Veterans Health Administration.

The incumber is member of the team caring for a diverse group of Veterans in various stages of the life cycle. The incumbent executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex patient care.

The incumbent is responsible for the documented outcomes at the program or service level. Major duties include, but are not limited to the following: Provide leadership and service excellence in patient throughput with oversight of the day to day operations of the Patient Flow Department.

Leadership responsibilities also include personnel management for Utilization Management, patient placement staff, Nurse Supervisors and patient support services, (i.e., intermittent and float pool staff).

Direct the system-wide Bed Management System (BMS) and Emergency Department Integration System (EDIS) including integration with other support departments. You will provide appropriate reports to monitor patient throughput initiatives within the organization.

Collaborates with all disciplines to ensure that the discharge/transfer of patients is achieved in a way that meets the needs of the patient and complies with priorities for action targets.

Collaborates with clinical teams in ensuring that all patients requiring admission are placed in the most appropriate clinical environment available within the four-hour standard. Demonstrates competence in current knowledge of specific unit placement criteria (i.e., BMS, EDIS).

Analyzes performance of patient throughput systems and protocols using critical thinking skills. Demonstrates and communicates commitment to performance improvement through unit-based teams and a culture of engagement.

Standardize communications and expectations across disciplines Establish and enforce standard work for nursing care that is consistent, clear, and available to staff. Utilizes patient flow technology to help teams focus on common goals. Ensures that appropriate resources and processes are in place to manage and maintain new technologies.

Responsible for direct coordination of staffing, physical facilities, supplies and equipment for nursing services to patients on a 24 hour, 7 day a week basis.

Manages the delivery of quality patient care, including accurate and appropriate documentation, employees clinical/performance competency and continuous National and VANCHCS Performance Improvement Measures, consistent with VANCHCS mission. Accountable for successfully building and reinforcing essential programs.

Serves as a change agent and actively participates in systematically evaluating existing programs, planning new programs, and implementing changes in clinical standards of care. Implements action plans to effect positive change.

Oversees and monitors employee's adherence to VHA Privacy/HIPPA and Information Security Responsible for retention and recruitment of highly skilled nursing staff, monitoring changes in work flow, technical and equipment needs, and ensuring a workforce that can adapt to a rapidly changing environment.

Provides oversight to ensure that standards of practice are met within the department. Assures nursing competencies are developed and implemented to ensure competence in providing care. Responsible for ensuring employees complete mandatory annual and on time facility and nursing training and reviews within mandated time frame.

Responsible for ensuring annual appraisals/proficiencies are completed, communicated to the employees and submitted in a timely manner. Manages and reinforces VANCHCS time and leave policies. Ensures time management procedures are followed accurately.

The role of a Charge Nurse "aims to enhance nurse retention, bolster teamwork, improve patient safety, and raise overall quality of care." They function as a role model, educator, while providing guidance to the team.

Duties include but are not limited to: In collaboration with the Nurse Manager, functions as an operational lead and assumes accountability for the operation of all areas within the role Serve as the operational lead for the nursing team to ensure that clinics run smoothly and that patient care needs are met in a coordinated, timely manner Lead staff by coordinating care, supporting staff, and responding quickly when unexpected challenges arise Contributing to the establishment and implementation of evidence-based nursing standards of practice.

Accountable for adhering to established policies, standards of care and standards of practice, demonstrating leadership in improving nursing care, as well as other duties as assigned. Providing direct patient care by assessing patient needs and making clinical decisions by monitoring patient conditions and responding to changes.

Coordinating treatment plans and ensuring correct execution while collaborating with physicians and other members of care teams to refine care strategies.

Administering medications and performing procedures as needed Assigning clinic duties to nursing staff based on acuity and staff skill levels Providing guidance and mentorship to newer or less experienced staff Acting as a liaison between the nursing team and other departments Stepping in to resolve conflicts or clarify orders when delays occur Informing Veterans and their families about unit procedures or status changes Reporting staffing changes or concerns, managing supplies and ensuring necessary equipment is available, responding to documentation needs, including chart audits to ensure accuracy while ensuring compliance with evidenced based practice for infection control and safety standards Reporting incidents or quality concerns to leadership and follow through with steps to resolve and ensure safe quality care.

Champions Peer to Peer Chart Audit process Inspecting clinics for environmental safety and cleanliness compliance, maintains list of work orders from entry to resolution.

The Registered Nurse (RN) in the Medical Surgical Day Unit (MSDU) provides comprehensive pre-operative and procedural nursing care for patients undergoing Interventional Radiology, MRI, and surgical procedures at the West Roxbury campus.

The RN also administers infusion therapies such as IVIG and may float to the Ambulatory Surgery Unit in Jamaica Plain as needed. This role requires strong clinical judgment, independent practice, and effective collaboration with interdisciplinary teams to ensure safe, high-quality patient care throughout all phases of the peri-procedural experience.

The RN serves as a patient advocate and supports clinical, administrative, educational, and research aspects of the service. Deliver comprehensive pre-operative and procedural nursing care for Operating Room, Interventional Radiology, and MRI patients.

Perform full nursing assessments; validate consents and H&P documentation; initiate IV access/venipuncture; and complete required pre-procedure testing. Verify accuracy of surgical site preparation, marking, and patient consent. Administer medications as ordered and monitor patient responses.

Provide clear pre-operative teaching and review discharge instructions with patients and families. Monitor post-operative patients recovering from anesthesia or sedation, assessing for side effects or complications. Maintain knowledge of ASPAN standards, VHA directives, and service-level SOPs.

Document all phases of care accurately and promptly in the electronic health record. Function independently and serve as Charge Nurse when assigned. Provide guidance and education to students and newly onboarded staff. Apply the nursing process to coordinate evidence-based, interdisciplinary care focused on health promotion and disease prevention.

Participate in quality-improvement initiatives to enhance patient care and workflow efficiency. Collaborate on patient-flow processes including Travel, Housing, and Chaperone coordination. Provide clinic coverage as assigned and maintain required procedural and core competencies.

Support patient care throughout the entire visit from check-in through discharge. Demonstrate strong communication skills and professional behaviors that support teamwork and collaboration with colleagues and patients. Work Schedule: Monday-Friday, 10:30 A.M.-7 P.M. or 9:30 A.M.-6 P.M.

Vous menez des consultations individuelles (prises de sang et tests diagnostiques, traitement, organisation des suivis) chez des patients et patientes porteurs de pathologies endocriniennes.

s.h: Les pathologies que vous pourrez rencontrer sont
s.t:
Maladies de la thyroïde (hyperthyroïdie, hypothyroïdie, nodule thyroïdien, goitre, cancer)

Maladies de la surrénale (syndrome de Cushing, insuffisance surrénalienne, tumeurs surrénaliennes)
Maladies des ovaires et des testicules (hirsutisme, gynécomastie, syndrome des ovaires polykystiques, hypogonadisme, infertilité)

Vous êtes motivé ou motivée à acquérir les connaissances spécifiques liées aux pathologies prises en charge dans le service afin de garantir une prise en charge optimale des patients et patientes.
Vous faites preuve d’excellentes compétences relationnelles, avec un sens aigu de l’accueil, de l’écoute, du non\-jugement, de l’empathie, de la bienveillance et du calme.

Enfin, vous êtes autonome et disposez d’un excellent sens du relationnel, favorisant une collaboration de qualité avec les patients et les équipes.
Vous avez une excellente maîtrise de la langue française tant à l’orale qu’à l’écrit.

s.t:
Health System Shared Services | Revenue Cycle Clinical Support Scope of Position
Revenue Cycle Clinical Support Office (RCCS) is an area within Access and Revenue Cycle Management Shared Services responsible for Clinical Pre-Certification, Case Reviews, Pre-billing edits, in-patient account validations, supporting Utilization Management, Peer to Peer processes, complex billing scenarios, audits (governmental, commercial, compliance, and internal), clinical appeals and denial management.

RCCS is integral to the Revenue Cycle and supports cash collection through preventing and appealing denials.

The Clinical Financial Case Manager - RN (CFCM-RN) implements and supports the philosophy, mission, values, standards, policies, and procedures of The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. The CFCM-RN functions within the multidisciplinary team to secure complex pre-authorizations and prevent/appeal clinical denials.

The job duties require the utilization of clinical knowledge to interpret and apply medical necessity guidelines to determine appropriateness for services provided. The CFCM-RN makes determinations on the appropriate level of care (Inpatient or Observation) based on the ability to read, understand, and interpret documented clinical
information. The role requires CFCM-RNs to become Subject Matter Experts (SME) for assigned payers as well as governmental payer requirements and audits such as RAC, MAC, QIO, etc. The CFCM-RN maintains an awareness of State and National Health care trends, JCAHO, CMS, and third-party payer Utilization Management guidelines.
The Financial aspect of the role involves acquiring knowledge of Managed Care, Scheduling, Financial Counseling, Pre-Certification, Admissions/Discharges/Transfers, Clinical workflows and documentation, Revenue Management, Charge Description Master, Coding (Diagnosis, HCPCS, Revenue Codes, Procedure Codes, Modifiers, etc.), Medical Information Management, Release of Information, Case Management, Utilization Management, Clinical Documentation Improvement, Compliance, Legal, Finance, Transplant workflows, Billing, Follow Up, Cash Posting, and any other areas that maybe needed to complete the tasks.

The CFCM-RN must be able to read, understand and interpret a payer remit, denial/remark codes, and expected reimbursement to determine the cost effectiveness of completing an appeal.
The CFCM-RN must be versatile, flexible, and very adaptable to change because the payer rules change constantly. The CFCM-RN must be able to troubleshoot, problem solve, continuously learn, be highly independent, self-motivated and have an elevated level of interpretive skills and the ability to work closely with departments such as Legal, Medical Information Management, Physician groups and the Business Office.

Bachelor’s degree in nursing with current license required.
Minimum of 3 years clinical care experience, caring for patients, anticipating their needs, and understanding the physician’s
plan of care.
Experience collaborating with physicians and their designees.
Strong, proven analytical skills. Ability to make educated decisions.
Extensive knowledge of clinical operations and patient flow.
Skilled at synthesizing large volumes of information and concisely communicating either verbally or in writing.
Proficient in Microsoft Office Products such as: Word, Power Point, Excel, SharePoint, Teams, OneNote, etc.
Proficient in Adobe Professional Proficient in using email, fax machines, copy machines, internet browsers.
Proficient at typing
Proficient in Technology, Computer, and Web applications. Must be able to multitask and move between applications quickly and frequently. Must be able to orientate self to new applications quickly. Must be able to manage complexities of having to work in multiple applications such as IHIS, MS Office products, 3M, and all payer websites/applications.

The Emergency Department (ED) Registered Nurse (RN) executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex patient care. Collaborates in the development, implementation, evaluation, and revision of policies, procedures, and/or guidelines.

Provides urgent and emergent care to patients with acute and/or chronic medical, surgical, and psychiatric conditions. Nursing care ranges from basic nursing care to stabilization, resuscitation, and life support measures. Emergency nursing practice is independent and collaborative.

The ED RN practice includes the roles of direct care provider, educator, administrator, researcher, consultant, leader, and advocate. Provides peers with formal or informal constructive feedback for improvement. Supports colleagues and other nurses through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care.

Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of health care professionals. Evaluates outcomes of evidence-based decisions and practice changes for individuals, groups, and populations. Responsible for the documented outcomes at the program or service level.

Program or service level outcomes must be broad and complex and can be demonstrated at any organizational level within a facility. The ED RN is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing care.

They assess the patient by collecting pertinent data or information, including the triage of patients based on the five-level triage system to prioritize patients that require more immediate care. They use the assessment data to determine diagnoses, problems, or other concerns.

They will identify expected outcomes to develop a collaborative and individualized plan for each patient. The ED RN will implement that plan, including care coordination, health teaching, and health promotion. They evaluate the progress toward achieving the expected goal and outcomes and adjusts the plan as necessary.

Im Einsatz arbeitest du mit Patienten, und gleichzeitig triffst du schnelle Entscheidungen, sodass jede Situation gut gemeistert wird.
· Du nimmst Patienten auf und schätzt die Lage ein, sodass klar ist, was zuerst gemacht wird
· Du leitest erste Maßnahmen ein, damit die Versorgung sofort beginnt
· Du überwachst Patienten, sodass du Veränderungen früh erkennst
· Du arbeitest mit Ärzten zusammen, damit alles gut abgestimmt ist
· Du handelst im Notfall direkt, sodass Patienten geschützt sind
· Du erklärst Angehörigen die Situation, damit Vertrauen entsteht
